Q_001,How do I get help for food like SNAP or other places?,"## Getting Food Help in California
You’ve lost your job and need help putting food on the table. Below are the main ways Californians get food assistance, what you need to qualify, and the simple steps to apply.
### 1. CalFresh (California’s SNAP program)

column3: Monthly money put on an **EBT card** that you can use at grocery stores to buy most foods.

• Adults (18+) who live in California.
• Families with children.
• Seniors (60+) or people with disabilities.
• Income must be at most about 200 % of the federal poverty level (the exact number changes each year).

• Photo ID (driver’s license, state ID, or passport).
• Proof of California residence (utility bill, lease, or mail addressed to you).
• Recent pay stubs, unemployment benefits statement, or other income documents.
• Social Security numbers for everyone in the household.

1. **Online** – Go to **[GetCalFresh.org](https://www.getcalfresh.org)** or **BenefitsCal.com** and click “Apply now.”
2. **Phone** – Call the CalFresh Helpline **1‑877‑847‑3663** for help and to request a paper application.
3. **In‑person** – Visit your **County Social Services Agency** (the location varies by county).
4. **Assistance** – If you need help filling out the form, dial **2‑1‑1** or call the helpline; many agencies have staff who can walk you through it.
Most people hear back within **30 days**. If you qualify for emergency benefits (e.g., you’re homeless or have a medical emergency), you may receive **partial benefits in as few as 3 days**.

Search “California County Social Services” or click the “Contact Your County Social Services Agency” link on the CalFresh website. Remember: **rules and application processes can vary a little by county**.

column1: ### 2. Women, Infants & Children (WIC)

column3: Free nutrition program for pregnant people, new moms, infants, and children up to age 5.

• Low‑income families (usually ≤ 185 % of the federal poverty level).
• Must meet state‑specific nutrition risk criteria.
Call **1‑800‑942‑3670** or visit your local **County Health Department**. You can also apply online in many counties via the WIC website.
Vouchers for milk, cheese, fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and infant formula, plus nutrition counseling.

column1: ### 3. Emergency Food Assistance Program (EFAP)

column3: Federal program that provides **free meals or food boxes** at local food banks and community centers.
Anyone with low or no income. No application needed at most sites; you just show proof of residence (e.g., a piece of mail).

Use the **[California Food Bank Locator](https://www.cdss.ca.gov/food-banks)** to find the nearest pantry, soup kitchen, or community center. Call the phone number listed for your county if you need directions.

### 5. Additional Supports You Might Need

column3: **Program that can help**
Look into **Medi‑Cal** (California’s Medicaid) or local free‑clinic programs. See **[USA.gov – Help with Medical Bills](https://www.usa.gov/help-with-medical-bills)** for details.
The **Weatherization Assistance Program (WAP)** offers free home‑energy upgrades for low‑income households. Check your local WAP office.
Call **2‑1‑1** or the **HUD Homeless Assistance List** for shelter referrals. The **National Runaway Hotline (1‑800‑786‑2929)** also helps youth.
**CalWORKs** (California’s TANF program) provides cash aid, job‑search help, and training. Contact your County Social Services Agency to ask about CalWORKs services.

column1: ## Quick “What‑to‑Do” Checklist

column3: What to do
ID, proof of residence, income statements (pay stubs, unemployment notice, SSI, etc.), Social Security numbers.
Online at **GetCalFresh.org**, phone the helpline, or visit your county office.
Ask for the nearest **food bank**, **EFAP pantry**, and any **emergency housing** referrals.
If you have a young child or are pregnant, call **1‑800‑942‑3670**.
After you submit an application, note the case number and call back if you haven’t heard within 30 days.
Save copies of all forms and any letters you receive. This makes it easier to appeal or reapply later.

column1: ### You’re Not Alone

Losing a job is stressful, but many **Californians** are just a phone call or a few clicks away from food assistance. If you ever feel stuck, **dial 2‑1‑1**—the line is free, works 24/7, and can connect you with a social‑service counselor who will walk you through each step.
*Remember: each county may have slightly different paperwork or office hours, so be sure to check with your local agency.*

Q_002,Can I recieve multiple types of assistance at the same time?,"## Quick Answer

**Yes – you can often get more than one state or federal benefit at the same time**, as long as each program’s rules allow it. Many people receive a mix of cash help, food assistance, health coverage, and utility help together.
## How It Works

column1: **Bottom line:** Most programs are designed to stack, so you can get help for food, health, housing, utilities, and phone/internet all at once. The only time you might be blocked is if two programs try to pay for the exact same thing (for example, two separate cash‑aid programs that both count the same income).
## Steps to Get Multiple Benefits
1. **Gather basic info** – ID, Social Security number, proof of California residence (like a lease or utility bill), and recent pay stubs or bank statements.
2. **Apply for the biggest need first** – many people start with **Unemployment Insurance (UI)** if they qualify, then add **Medi‑Cal**, **CalFresh**, and **CalWORKs** or **General Assistance**.

3. **Tell each agency about the other benefits** – when you fill out an application, there will be a question like “Do you receive any other public assistance?” Answer “Yes” and list them. This avoids delays.
4. **Submit required documents** – most programs need:
* Photo ID (driver’s license, state ID, or passport)
* Proof of income (pay stubs, unemployment award letter, or a letter showing you have no income)
* Proof of residency (lease, utility bill, or mail addressed to you)
* Benefit letters from any program you already receive (e.g., SNAP award notice) – these prove you qualify for Lifeline, etc.
5. **Get a case manager** – the county social services office can guide you through each application and make sure the programs don’t overlap incorrectly.
6. **Follow up** – most agencies will call or mail you within 2‑4 weeks. Keep a notebook of dates, contact names, and what you sent.

## County‑Specific Note

Every California county runs its own **social services office**. While the basic rules are the same statewide, **some counties may have extra programs, different income‑test calculators, or faster processing times**. For example, Alameda County offers online, phone, mail, in‑person, and fax options for General Assistance (see Source 8). Check the website or call your county’s Department of Social Services to learn about local variations.
## Other Programs You Might Need
- **Emergency Rental Assistance** – ask 211 or your county for short‑term rent help (Source 23).
- **Housing Vouchers (Section 8, public housing)** – apply through the local public housing agency (Source 10).
- **SSI or SSDI** – if you’re 65+, blind, or disabled, you may qualify for federal SSI; the county can help you file (Source 9, 18).
- **Veterans’ Benefits** – veterans can add pension or survivor benefits to qualify for Lifeline or other aid (Source 1, 11).
- **CAPI (Cash Assistance for Immigrants)** – if you’re a non‑citizen age 65+ and meet residency rules (Source 4, 18).
## Helpful Links
- **Apply for Unemployment**: [EDD – Unemployment UI](https://edd.ca.gov/en/unemployment/) (Source 24)
- **Medi‑Cal & CalFresh**: [Covered California / CalFresh](https://www.coveredca.com)
- **CalWORKs**: Apply online at **BenefitsCal.com** or contact your county (Source 6)
- **General Assistance (GA)**: Online portal or phone for Alameda County (Source 8)
- **LIHEAP**: Find your local agency here → [LIHEAP Agency Search](https://www.csd.ca.gov/Pages/LIHEAPProgram.aspx) (Source 5, 21)
- **Lifeline**: Check eligibility and apply → [California Lifeline FAQ](https://www.californialifeline.com/en/faq) (Source 12)
## Bottom Line

You **can receive several types of assistance at once**—food, health, cash, utility, and communication benefits often stack together. Start with the programs that address your most urgent need, keep all your paperwork organized, and let your county social services office guide you through the process.
*If you have any specific questions about what you qualify for, call your local social services office or dial 211 for free, confidential help.*

Q_004,How can I get help with rent?,"## How to Get Help Paying Your Rent in California
Losing a job can make it hard to keep up with rent. Below are the main ways you can get money or other help, what you usually need to qualify, and the steps to apply.
### 1. **Emergency Rental Assistance (ERA)**
A state‑wide program that gives short‑term cash to help you catch up on past‑due rent, utilities, or security deposits.

column3: **Who may qualify**
column4: **Typical timeline**

column3: California residents who lost income because of unemployment, reduced hours, or COVID‑19‑related reasons. You must show the rent is **more than 30 % of your income**.
column4: Applications are reviewed in **2‑4 weeks** after you submit all required paperwork.

column1: #### How to apply
1. **Call your local 211** (dial **2‑1‑1**) or visit the 211 website.
2. Tell them you need *emergency rental assistance*. They will give you the phone number or web link for your county’s ERA program.
3. **Gather documents** (see the list below).
4. Fill out the online or paper application and send it back.
> **Note:** Each county runs its own ERA program, so the exact forms and deadlines can differ.
### 2. **CalWORKs (California Work Opportunity and Responsibility to Kids)**
Provides cash aid to families with low income, which can be used for rent, utilities, food, and other needs.
#### Who can apply
- You are a California resident.
- You have children under 19 (or 21 if they’re a student or disabled).
- Your household income is below the **state’s low‑income limit** (the exact number varies by county).
#### Steps
1. Call your **County Human Services Agency** (find the number on the CDSS website or by dialing 2‑1‑1).
2. Complete an intake interview (in person, by phone, or online).
3. Provide proof of identity, residence, and income (see the document list).
#### What you get
- Monthly cash payments that can be used for rent.
- Help with utilities, child care, and job‑training services.
### 3. **Local Non‑Profit & Community Organizations**
Many charities, churches, and community groups have rent‑relief funds or can give you a one‑time cash grant.
#### How to find them
- Call **211** and ask for “non‑profit rent assistance in my area.”
- Search online for “rent assistance + *your county name*.”
- Visit a local **food bank** or **community center**; they often have a list of partner organizations.
These groups may have separate eligibility rules (often based on income and need) and may be able to help faster than state programs.
### 4. **Utility & Energy Help (LIHEAP & WAP)**
If your rent includes large utility bills, you might qualify for the **Low‑Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP)** or the **Weatherization Assistance Program (WAP)**.
- **LIHEAP**: Helps pay heating, cooling, or electric bills.
- **WAP**: Provides free home‑weather‑proofing (insulation, sealing) that can lower future utility costs.
**How to apply:** Call your county’s **LIHEAP office** (search “LIHEAP *your county*”) or call **2‑1‑1** for the phone number.
### 5. **HUD‑Approved Housing Counseling**
A HUD counselor can review your situation, talk to your landlord, and suggest payment‑plan options.
- Call the **HOPE Hotline** at **(888) 995‑HOPE (4673)** 24/7.
- Ask for a **HUD‑approved housing counseling agency** near you (search “HUD housing counseling *your zip code*”).
Counselors can also point you to local rental‑assistance programs you might have missed.

URL: https://www.getcalfresh.org/en/faq

You can definitely apply for CalFresh if you just lost your job. If your income recently stopped, your county will only count any final payments you got in the last 30 days to calculate how much CalFresh you will receive in the first month. If you still have any income, your ongoing benefits will be based only on that income, not income that has stopped. You should provide proof of any money you got in the last 30 days if you can.

It isn't required, but it can be helpful to provide any proof you have that your income has stopped. This could be a letter, or a screenshot of an email or text from your employer that explains that you are no longer working. If you can’t get proof, write a letter that explains that you aren’t working. Make sure to include the last date you worked, and sign and date it.

Q_006,How do I apply for Medi-Cal after a layoff?,"## You’ve Lost Your Job – What to Do Next for **Medi‑Cal**

I’m sorry you’re dealing with a layoff. You may still qualify for health coverage right away. Below is a simple guide that walks you through the basics, who can apply, what you need, and how to get started.
## 1. What Is Medi‑Cal?
- **Medi‑Cal** is California’s public health‑insurance program (a part of Medicaid).
- It can give you **free or low‑cost doctor visits, prescriptions, hospital stays, and more**.
- If you’ve lost your job and your income is low, you are often eligible right away.
## 2. Who May Be Eligible After a Layoff?

column3: What It Means for You

Your household income (including the last pay you received) must be at or below about **138 % of the Federal Poverty Level**. The exact dollar amount changes each year, but the state will use the most recent numbers when you apply.
The more people you support (spouse, kids, parents), the higher the income limit.
You must live in California.
U.S. citizens, Permanent Residents, and many other lawfully‑present immigrants can qualify. Some other immigrant groups may qualify for limited‑benefit Medi‑Cal.
If you already get **CalFresh (food stamps), CalWORKs, SSI, or other state assistance**, you automatically qualify for Medi‑Cal.
If you have a disability, the income test is higher, and the state can decide faster.

Q_007,What are the income limits for Unemployment Insurance?,"## What “Income Limits” Mean for Unemployment Insurance (UI)
### Quick answer
**Unemployment Insurance does not have a fixed income‑limit you must stay under.**

Instead, you qualify and get a weekly payment based on **how much you earned in the “base period”** (the first four of the last five completed quarters). The more you earned, the higher your weekly benefit – up to a state maximum.
## How UI Works in Simple Steps

column4: Why it matters

column3: Find your recent pay stubs, W‑2 forms, or a record of wages for the past 12‑18 months.
column4: UI looks at these wages to decide if you’re eligible and how much you’ll get.

column3: File online at **myEDD → UI Online**, by phone, or by mailing Form DE 1101I.
column4: The claim starts the process; you’ll get an EDD Customer Account Number in about 10 business days.

column3: Log in each week and answer a few questions (Did you work? Did you earn any money?).
column4: Certification tells EDD you’re still unemployed and keeps the benefits flowing.

column3: Payments are deposited onto a debit card or direct‑deposit account, usually 1‑2 weeks after you certify.

column1: ## What Determines Your UI Benefit Amount?

column3: How it’s used
EDD adds up your earnings and calculates an “average weekly wage.”
In 2025 the highest weekly UI benefit in California is about **$450** (exact amount can change each year).
If you pick up a part‑time job, you can still get a reduced benefit.

column1: > **Bottom line:** There is no “income ceiling” that blocks you from getting UI. If you earned **any wages** in the base period, you will likely qualify, but the exact weekly amount depends on how much you earned.
## Who Is Eligible? (Simple checklist)
- You **lost your job** or had your hours cut **through no fault of your own** (layoff, company closure, etc.).
- You are **physically able, available, and actively looking for work** each week.
- You have earned **enough wages** in the base period (usually at least a few weeks of work; the exact dollar amount changes each year but is not a strict “limit”).
- You are a **U.S. citizen, permanent resident, or eligible non‑citizen**.
If you’re not sure, **apply anyway** – EDD will tell you if you meet the requirements.

column1: ## How to Know If You May Qualify
1. **Check Your Income**
- Look at your most recent pay stub, unemployment check, or benefits statement.
- Compare it to the **Federal Poverty Level (FPL)**. For a single adult, 138 % FPL is about **$24,000** a year in 2025. (Exact numbers can change, so ask your county.)
2. **Confirm Your Residency**
- You must live in California. Some counties require you to have lived there **≥ 15 days** (e.g., Alameda).
3. **Check Immigration Status**
- U.S. citizens, permanent residents, and many qualified non‑citizens (including refugees, asylees, and certain undocumented adults with a *Qualified Immigrant Status*) can get Medi‑Cal.
4. **Look for Other Qualifying Programs**
- If you already receive **SNAP (CalFresh), SSI, or Federal Public Housing Assistance**, you automatically qualify for many other benefits (Lifeline, LIHEAP, WAP, etc.).

column1: ### Basic Steps (Same for all ways)
1. **Create a BenefitsCal account** (if applying online).
2. **Complete the CalWORKs application (CW‑1)** – answer questions about who lives with you, your income, any assets, and your work history.
3. **Gather required documents** (see the list below).
4. **Submit the application** online, in person, by phone, or by mail.
5. **Talk with a caseworker** – they may ask for more info or schedule a meeting.
6. **Wait for a decision** – most counties respond within a few weeks, but timing can vary.
### What You’ll Need to Provide

column3: **Examples**
Driver’s license, state ID, or passport.
Lease, utility bill, or a letter from a landlord.
Recent pay stubs, unemployment award notice, or a letter from a benefits agency.
Bank statements, vehicle registration, or proof of ownership of property.
Birth certificates, school enrollment letters, or custody papers.
Green card, work permit, or other immigration documents.

column1: *If you’re not sure which documents you need, the county worker will tell you.*
### Eligibility Quick Check (Simple Overview)

column3: **What It Means**

column2: You have a child **under 18** (or are pregnant)
column3: The program is for families with kids or expecting a baby.
Income limits differ by county, but most families earn less than the state average.

column2: You have **limited assets** (like savings or a car)
column3: The program looks at both income and what you own.
Most people who can stay in the U.S. can apply; some undocumented families may qualify for limited help.

column1: > **Note:** Exact income and asset limits **vary by county**, so talk to your local office to see the numbers that apply to you.
### Timelines

column3: **Typical Timeframe**
Immediate (online) or when you deliver the paper form
1–2 weeks (varies by county)
Up to 1 week after they contact you
Usually within **30 days** of a complete application

column1: ### Other Programs That Might Help You
- **CalFresh (Food Stamps)** – provides monthly benefits for groceries. Apply at **BenefitsCal.com** or your county office.
- **Medi‑Cal** – free or low‑cost health insurance for low‑income families.
- **California Work Opportunity and Responsibility to Kids (CalWORKs) Child‑Care Services** – helps pay for child‑care while you look for work.
- **Unemployment Insurance (UI)** – if you lost a job through no fault of your own, you can file a claim at **[myEDD.gov](https://myedd.ca.gov)**.

- **Women, Infants, and Children (WIC)** – nutrition program for pregnant moms, new parents, and kids under 5. Find a local office on the **[WIC website](https://www.cdph.ca.gov/Programs/CFH/DWICSN/Pages/HowCanIGetWIC.aspx)**.
### Quick Tips
- **Start online** – it’s the fastest way and you can upload documents right away.
- **Keep copies** of everything you send.
- **Ask for help** – county staff, community “Benefits” centers, and the BenefitsCal live chat can walk you through each step.
- **Don’t give up** – if you’re denied, you have the right to ask for a hearing or to re‑apply with new information.

**You’re not alone.**  Applying for benefits can feel overwhelming, but many families in California have gone through the same process and gotten the help they need. Take one step at a time, and reach out to your county social services office if you hit a roadblock. Q_010,What documents do I need for Unemployment Insurance and how do I apply?,"## Quick Overview

Unemployment Insurance (UI) gives a short‑term cash payment to people in California who lose their job **through no fault of their own**. The payment is meant to help you pay bills while you look for a new job or go to training.
## Who Can Apply? *(Eligibility Basics)*

column3: What it means for you
You earned enough wages during the “base period” (the first 4 quarters of the last 18 months).
You are totally or partially unemployed **and** the loss was not your fault (e.g., layoff, reduced hours).
You are physically able, available for work, looking for a job each week, and willing to accept work right away.
You have a Social Security number and are authorized to work in the U.S. (if you’re not a citizen, you’ll need immigration documents).
You live in California.  *Specific rules can differ a bit by county, so check with your local America’s Job Center.*

column1: > **Tip:** Even if you’re not sure you qualify, **apply anyway**. The EDD will tell you if you meet the rules.
## What Documents Do You Need?

column3: Why it’s needed
Identifies you in the system.

column2: **Valid ID** (driver’s license, state ID, or passport)
column3: Proves identity.

column2: **Recent pay stubs or wage statements** (last 2‑3 pay periods)
column3: Shows how much you earned.
Needed for the EDD to verify your job loss.
Lets the EDD send your money fast.

column2: **Proof of work‑authorization (if not a U.S. citizen)** – e.g., green card, work permit, visa, or SAVE verification
column3: Confirms you can legally work in the U.S.
Shows you’re looking for work online.

column2: **Any letters about job loss** (e.g., layoff notice, termination letter) – helpful but not required
column3: Provides extra proof if the EDD asks.

column1: *If you can’t get a document right away, you can often **self‑attest** in writing, but the EDD may ask for the original later.*
## How to Apply
### 1. Gather Your Documents
Put the items above together in a folder (paper or digital).
### 2. Choose an Application Method

column3: How to Do It
column4: Speed

column3: Go to **[myEDD UI portal](https://edd.ca.gov/en/unemployment/)**, create a myEDD account, and follow the “Apply for UI” prompts.
column4: Fast – you’ll get a confirmation email right away.

column3: Call **1‑800‑300‑5616** (English self‑service) or **1‑800‑547‑2058** for other languages. Interpreter services are free.
column4: Same‑day start, but wait times can be long.

column3: Fill out the paper form **DE 1101I** (available on the EDD site) and mail or fax it to the address on the form.
column4: Takes longer (weeks).

column3: Visit your local **America’s Job Center of California** for free help with the paper application.
column4: Helpful if you need personal assistance.

column1: ### 3. Register for CalJOBS
After you file your claim, you’ll be asked to create a free account at **[CalJOBS.org](https://www.caljobs.ca.gov/)** and upload a résumé. This shows you’re actively looking for work.
### 4. Review Your Benefit Statement
The EDD will send you a **Welcome/Benefit Letter** (by mail or email) that tells you:
* Your weekly benefit amount (usually $40‑$450).
* Your **EDD Customer Account Number** (10‑digit code).
### 5. Certify for Benefits Each Week
*Log in to myEDD* or call **1‑866‑333‑4606** (Tele‑Cert) every two weeks to answer simple questions:
- Did you work or earn any money?
- Are you still looking for work?
If you skip certification, you won’t get a payment for that period.
### 6. First Payment Timeline
- **Processing time:** About **3 weeks** from when the EDD finishes your application.
- **Payment frequency:** Every **2 weeks** after you certify.
If you have any problems (e.g., a request for more info, a phone interview, or a notice of overpayment), the EDD will contact you by **email, mail, or phone**. Respond quickly to avoid delays.
## Other Programs You Might Qualify For

column3: What it Helps With
column4: How to Apply

column3: Cash aid for families with children or adults with low income.
column4: Apply at your local County social services office or online at **[benefitscal.com](https://benefitscal.com/)**.

column3: Food vouchers for groceries.
column4: Apply online at **[GetCalFresh.org](https://www.getcalfresh.org/)** or at a County office.

column3: Free or low‑cost health insurance.
column4: Apply online at **[CoveredCA.com](https://www.coveredca.com/)** or through your County office.

column3: Allows you to attend school or job‑training while still receiving UI.
column4: Ask the EDD when you certify or check the UI portal.

column3: If you become disabled while unemployed, you may get state disability benefits.
column4: File a claim with the EDD’s DI program.

column1: ## Important Reminders

* **County differences:** Some counties have extra paperwork or local outreach programs. Call your **County Human Services Agency** or visit a local **America’s Job Center** to learn about any special rules.
* **No guarantee:** Providing the right documents and following the steps does **not guarantee** that you will receive benefits or a certain amount.
* **Avoid overpayments:** Only claim weeks you truly qualify for. If you’re paid by mistake, the EDD will send a **Notice of Overpayment** and you can appeal.
* **Keep copies:** Save all forms, emails, and letters for at least one year.
## Need More Help?

- **Phone Help:** Call **1‑800‑300‑5616** (English) or **1‑800‑547‑2058** (other languages).
- **In‑Person Help:** Find your nearest **America’s Job Center of California** [here](https://www.caljobs.ca.gov/).

Q_011,Laid off this month. I need help paying for food. Can I get help quickly? What can I qualify for and how do I apply in my county?,"## You Lost Your Job – How to Get Food Help Fast
I’m sorry you’re going through this. Below are the main programs that can give you food money right away, plus a few other resources that might help while you look for a new job.
### 1. CalFresh (California’s SNAP program)

column3: Monthly food benefits that are put on an **EBT card** you can use at grocery stores.
Anyone who lives in California and has low or no income.  You can still qualify even if you just lost your job this month.

• Income ≤ about 200 % of the federal poverty level (the exact number changes each year).
• Must be a U.S. citizen, permanent resident, or have another qualifying immigration status.
• Must have a California address.

• Photo ID (driver’s licence, state ID, or passport).
• Social Security number (or proof you don’t have one).
• Proof of your recent income – last 30 days of pay stubs **or** a letter/email from your employer that says you were laid off and the last day you worked.
• Proof of where you live (lease, utility bill, or letter from a landlord).

1. Go to **[BenefitsCal.com](https://www.getcalfresh.org/en)** (or **www.benefitscal.com**) and click **“Apply for CalFresh.”**
2. Fill out the online form.
3. Your county will call you in 1‑2 weeks for an eligibility interview (phone or video).
4. Upload the documents above through the portal, or mail/bring them to the county office.
The county has **30 days** to approve or deny you. If you have very low income and few resources, you may qualify for **expedited service** (often within a few days).

• CalFresh Helpline: **1‑877‑847‑3663**

Q_015,Can you explain how unemployment insurance works and how to maximize what I can receive?,"## How Unemployment Insurance (UI) Works in California

column2: **Temporary cash help** while you look for a new job or wait for work to start again.
column3: You must be **totally or partially unemployed** through **no fault of your own** (e.g., laid off, hours cut). You also need to be **physically able, available, and willing to work** each week.
column4: A weekly payment between **$40 – $450** based on your earnings during the **base period** (the 12‑month window before you filed). Use the EDD’s **Unemployment Benefit Calculator** to get an estimate. *(Exact amount varies for each person.)*

column1: ### Key Things to Remember
- **You don’t have to be “perfectly” qualified** to apply. If you’re unsure, **apply now**. EDD will tell you if you meet the rules.
- Benefits are **temporary**. They keep coming each week **as long as you stay eligible** and keep certifying.
- You can **still go to school, training, or a job‑training program** while receiving UI (look into **California Training Benefits**).
## Who Can Apply?
You need to meet **all** of these basic rules:
1. **Social Security Number** (or ITIN if you have one).
2. **Authorization to work** in the U.S. (if you’re not a citizen).
3. **Earned enough wages** during the “base period” (the 12 months before you filed).
4. **Totally or partially unemployed** through no fault of your own.
5. **Physically able, available, and willing** to accept suitable work right away.
6. **Looking for work each week** (you’ll answer “yes” on the certification questionnaire).
> **Note:** Some details (like exact wage‑history requirements) can **vary by county**, so your local **America’s Job Center** or county UI office can give you the most exact guidance.
## Step‑by‑Step Guide to Getting UI

column3: While your claim is processing, **sign up for CalJOBS** (free job‑search site). This shows you’re looking for work.
column4: You can also get help from your local **America’s Job Center** to build a resume.

column3: After your claim is approved, the first payment usually arrives **about 3 weeks** after you filed. It’s deposited onto your **Money Network debit card**.
column4: Set up alerts in the Money Network app to know when money lands.

column3: Continue the certification process each 2‑week cycle. Benefits stop only if you’re no longer eligible, you quit the job search, or you reach the maximum weeks allowed.

URL: https://www.getcalfresh.org/en/faq

You can definitely apply for CalFresh if you just lost your job. If your income recently stopped, your county will only count any final payments you got in the last 30 days to calculate how much CalFresh you will receive in the first month. If you still have any income, your ongoing benefits will be based only on that income, not income that has stopped. You should provide proof of any money you got in the last 30 days if you can.

It isn't required, but it can be helpful to provide any proof you have that your income has stopped. This could be a letter, or a screenshot of an email or text from your employer that explains that you are no longer working. If you can’t get proof, write a letter that explains that you aren’t working. Make sure to include the last date you worked, and sign and date it.

Q_023,I’m getting a severance and might do part-time gig work. Can I still get unemployment and also Medi-Cal?,"## You’re Asking
**“I’m getting a severance and might do part‑time gig work. Can I still get unemployment and also Medi‑Cal?”**
Below is a friendly guide that explains what you need to know, what you’ll need to do, and other help that might be useful. All information is written at a 5th‑grade reading level.
## Quick Answer

column3: Answer (in short)

column2: **Can I get Unemployment Insurance (UI) while getting severance?**
column3: **Yes, usually –** but the amount of severance may reduce or pause your weekly UI benefits.

column2: **Can I work part‑time or do gig jobs and still get UI?**
column3: **Yes,** as long as you tell the state how much you earn each week. Your UI payment will be lowered by the amount you earn, but you can keep getting benefits.

column2: **Can I get Medi‑Cal at the same time?**
column3: **Yes,** if your total household income (including UI and any gig earnings) stays under the Medi‑Cal limit.  You can have both programs together.

column1: ## 1. Unemployment Insurance (UI)
### What UI Is
- A **temporary cash benefit** for people who lost work through no fault of their own.
- Paid **every week** after you finish the required paperwork.
### How Severance Affects UI
- **Severance is counted as income.**
- The state will look at how much severance you receive in the first 30 days and may **pause** UI payments until that money runs out.
- After the severance runs out, you can **start getting UI again** (or the pause may be very short).
### How Part‑Time or Gig Work Affects UI
- You **must report every dollar you earn** each week when you certify for benefits.
- UI will **reduce** your weekly benefit by the amount you earn **above a small allowance** (the allowance changes a little each year).
- You can **keep working** and still receive a reduced UI payment.
### Steps to Apply for UI

column3: What to Do
column4: Helpful Tips

column3:
• Social Security number
• Last employer’s name & address
• Dates you worked
• Your most recent pay stub
column4: Keep a notebook of all dates and numbers.

column3: Go to the **EDD (Employment Development Department) website** – https://edd.ca.gov/en/unemployment/
column4: The application is free and open 24/7.

column3: Create a CalJOBS account (required for most UI claims).
column4: This also helps you look for new jobs.

column3: Log in to your UI account and tell the state how much you earned (including gig work).
column4: Do this **by the due date** each week to avoid losing benefits.

column3: Save copies of any severance letters, gig invoices, or bank statements.
column4: If the EDD asks for proof, you’ll have it ready.

column1: ### Documents You May Need
- **Severance letter** (shows amount and dates).
- **Pay stubs or bank statements** that show the severance deposit.
- **Gig earnings statements** (e.g., PayPal, Venmo, or platform payout reports).
- **Proof of identity** (driver’s license, state ID, or passport).
### How Long It Takes
- The first UI payment usually arrives **about 2–3 weeks** after you finish the initial application and certify.
- If you have a severance pause, the payment may start **after the severance runs out**.
## 2. Medi‑Cal (California’s Medicaid)
### What Medi‑Cal Is
- **Free or low‑cost health coverage** for California residents who meet income limits.
- Covers doctor visits, hospital stays, prescriptions, and many preventive services.
### Income Rules
- **Household income** (including UI, severance, and gig earnings) must stay **under the Medi‑Cal limit** for your family size.
- The limit changes each year, so the exact dollar amount varies **by county**.
- If your income goes **above the limit**, you may still qualify for **Medi‑Cal “share of cost”** (you pay a small amount each month).
### Steps to Apply for Medi‑Cal

column3: What to Do
column4: Helpful Tips

column3: Use the online **Medi‑Cal eligibility tool** or call your County Social Services office.
column4: No penalty for checking; you’ll know right away if you qualify.

column3:
• ID (driver’s license, state ID)
• Proof of California residency (utility bill, lease)
• Recent pay stubs or UI award letter
• Severance letter
column4: If you don’t have a document, write a short letter explaining the situation.

column3: Apply **online at https://benefitscal.com**, **by phone**, **by mail**, or **in person** at your County Social Services office.
column4: Most counties accept online applications now.

column3: The state must decide **within 45 days** for most non‑disability applications (often faster).
column4: You’ll get a notice by mail or email.

column3: If approved, you’ll pick a managed‑care plan that works in your area.
column4: The plan will give you a member ID card.

column1: ### Documents You May Need
- **Proof of income** (UI award letter, severance letter, gig earnings).
- **Proof of residency** (lease, utility bill, or mortgage statement).
- **Proof of citizenship or eligible immigration status** (driver’s license, passport, green card).
### County‑Specific Note
- Every California county runs its own **Social Services Agency**.
- Some counties may ask for **extra paperwork** or have slightly different timelines.
- If you’re unsure, call your **County CalFresh / Medi‑Cal office** (the phone number is on the county’s website).
## 3. Can You Have Both UI and Medi‑Cal at the Same Time?
- UI payments are counted as **income** when the state decides your Medi‑Cal eligibility.
- As long as the total household income (UI + severance + gig earnings) stays **under the Medi‑Cal limit**, you’ll qualify for **full‑benefit Medi‑Cal**.
- If your income is a little above the limit, you might get Medi‑Cal with a **small monthly share of cost** (you still get affordable health coverage).

## 5. Quick Checklist for You
1. **Apply for UI** (online at the EDD website).
2. **Report your severance** when you first certify – it may pause UI for a short time.
3. **Report any gig earnings** each week; UI will be reduced but you stay eligible.
4. **Check Medi‑Cal eligibility** right away (online or phone).
5. **Gather required documents** (ID, residency proof, income proof).
6. **Apply for Medi‑Cal** (online at BenefitsCal or at your County office).
7. **Consider CalFresh, Lifeline, and LIHEAP** for extra support.
## 6. Where to Get Help
- **EDD (Unemployment)** – https://edd.ca.gov/en/unemployment/  (phone: 1‑800‑300‑5616)
- **Your County Social Services Office** – Find contact info at https://www.cdss.ca.gov/calworks#main-content
- **Medi‑Cal Help Line** – 1‑800‑541‑5555 (available 24/7)
- **CalFresh Hotline** – 1‑800‑282‑0023
### You’re Not Alone

Losing a job can feel scary, but California has many safety‑net programs. By applying for **UI**, **Medi‑Cal**, and other benefits, you can keep food on the table, stay healthy, and have some money while you look for your next opportunity.

If you run into any roadblocks, call the phone numbers above or ask a trusted friend or family member to help you fill out the forms. Losing a job can feel scary, especially when rent and utility bills are coming due. Below is a simple guide to the **emergency help you can apply for right now** while you wait for Unemployment Insurance (UI) to start.

column1: ## How to Get Emergency Rental Assistance (Quick Steps)
1. **Call 2‑1‑1** (or dial the 211 number for your county).
*You’ll talk to a real person who will ask about your income, family size, and where you live.*
2. **Gather these documents** (you may need them later):
- Proof of rent (lease or rent receipt)
- Recent utility bill(s)
- Photo ID (driver’s license, state ID, or passport)
- Recent pay stub or proof of unemployment (if you have it)
3. **Complete the application** – many counties let you apply **online** or **in person** at a community action agency.
4. **Wait for a decision** – most counties aim to respond within **2‑4 weeks**, but some give a **quick‑pay** (within a few days) for urgent cases.
## How to Apply for LIHEAP (Utility Help)
1. **Find your local LIHEAP office**:
- Go to the **[USA.gov LIHEAP page](https://www.usa.gov/help-with-energy-bills)** and click “Find help with LIHEAP.”
- Or call **2‑1‑1** and ask to be connected to the LIHEAP office for your county.
2. **Eligibility basics** (the same everywhere in California):
- Household income must be at or below about **150 % of the Federal Poverty Level** (exact number changes each year).
- You must be a **California resident** and have a **valid utility account**.
3. **What to bring**:
- Most recent **utility bill** (electric, gas, or water)
- **Proof of income** (pay stub, unemployment claim, or benefits award)
- **Photo ID**
4. **Timeline**:
- Applications are processed **within 1‑2 weeks** for emergency help (e.g., a disconnect notice).
- Regular assistance may take **3‑4 weeks**.

## Quick Checklist Before You Call
- [ ] **Write down** your rent amount, due date, and utility balances.
- [ ] Have **photo ID**, **lease**, and **latest utility bill** ready.
- [ ] Know your **social security number** and **recent employment dates** (for UI).
- [ ] Keep a **pen and paper** or a notes app to record names, phone numbers, and case numbers.
## Remember
- **Every county may have slightly different forms or extra programs**, so the 211 worker will tell you the exact steps for where you live.
- Applying for emergency rent help **does not affect** your right to UI benefits.
- It’s okay to ask for help more than once—if you’re denied today, you can appeal or try another local charity.
You’re taking the right steps by looking for help now. Stay hopeful, keep the paperwork organized, and reach out to 211 right away. Good luck, and take care of yourself!

You’re not alone – many people need extra help after a job loss. Below is a simple guide to start getting **food assistance (CalFresh)** and **health coverage (Medi‑Cal or Covered California)**.
### 1. Start with **CalFresh** (California’s SNAP program)

1. **Go to** [BenefitsCal.com](https://benefitscal.com) and click **“Apply for CalFresh.”**
2. Fill out the online questionnaire (you’ll need basic info about you, your income, and where you live).
3. After you submit, the San Francisco County Social Services Agency will call you for a short interview (usually within 7‑14 days).
column5: After the interview, most people hear back within **2‑3 weeks** whether they’re approved and how much benefit they’ll receive.

column1: **What you’ll need** (have these ready before you start):
* Photo ID (driver’s license, state ID, or passport)
* Social Security number (or proof you’re not eligible for one)
* Proof of residence (utility bill, lease, or a letter from a roommate)
* Proof of income (pay stubs, unemployment benefits notice, or a “no income” statement)
* Bank account information (for the EBT card to be linked)
**Tips**
* The interview is just to confirm the information you gave online. Be honest and ask the case worker to repeat anything you don’t understand.
* If you have a disability, you may be automatically eligible for higher benefits.
### 2. Get **Medi‑Cal** (California’s Medicaid) for Health Coverage

column5: Most people hear back **within 30 days**. If you need urgent care, ask the case worker about **“Emergency Medi‑Cal”** which can start right away.

* If you qualify for both CalFresh and Medi‑Cal, the two programs share information, so you only need to submit most documents once.

Q_027,"I was laid off, have kdis, and savings are low. For food stamps, can I get faster help and how does UI or severance affect eligibility? I might move countise soon to live with my mom to save money—what changes?","## Quick help for **CalFresh** (Food Stamps)

column3: Simple answer
Yes. If you apply now, the county usually sends a **conditional** benefit within **5‑10 days** after they finish your interview.

column2: **Will unemployment (UI) or severance change the amount?**
column3: UI money counts as **income**.  The more UI you get, the less CalFresh you may receive, but you can still qualify as long as the total income is under the program’s limit.  Severance pay is also counted as income the month you receive it.

column2: **Moving to another county (to live with Mom)?**
column3: Each county runs its own CalFresh office, so you will need to **re‑apply** in the new county.  The rules are similar, but the interview time and exact benefit amount can be a little different.  Tell the new county when you move so they can link your case.
Having children raises the income limit, so you’re more likely to get a larger benefit.

column2: **What if you haven’t worked for a while?**
column3: If you have no current earnings, only the UI or severance you receive will be counted.  You can still get CalFresh even if you are completely out of work.

column1: ### How to apply (simple steps)
1. **Create a myEDD account** (for UI) – you can do it online at [EDD UI Online](https://edd.ca.gov/en/unemployment/step-2-apply/).
2. **Start a CalFresh application** on [BenefitsCal.com](https://www.getcalfresh.org/en) (the site will forward you to your county).
3. **Schedule the eligibility interview** – the county will call you within a week or two. Answer the questions and be ready to give proof of income.

[Source 16] I just lost my job - how does that affect my application for CalFresh?
URL: https://www.getcalfresh.org/en/faq

You can definitely apply for CalFresh if you just lost your job. If your income recently stopped, your county will only count any final payments you got in the last 30 days to calculate how much CalFresh you will receive in the first month. If you still have any income, your ongoing benefits will be based only on that income, not income that has stopped. You should provide proof of any money you got in the last 30 days if you can.

It isn't required, but it can be helpful to provide any proof you have that your income has stopped. This could be a letter, or a screenshot of an email or text from your employer that explains that you are no longer working. If you can’t get proof, write a letter that explains that you aren’t working. Make sure to include the last date you worked, and sign and date it.
